exercise.name: Kneeling Hip Thrust

reference.title: Kneeling Hip Thrust (male)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip hinge from kneeling; knees and shins fixed)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the hips sit back, breathe out as you drive the hips forward to tall kneeling.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s back, short pause, 1.3 s forward

prescription.tempo: Sit back in about 2 s, pause, drive forward in about 1 s and squeeze
prescription.progression: A slow 3 s lowering, then a band anchored behind the hips or a weight held at the chest.

cues.text: Kneel tall on a mat, knees hip width, toes tucked, hands on the hips.
Breathe in and sit the hips back toward the heels while the chest tips forward; keep the back flat.
Breathe out and drive the hips forward until thighs and trunk are upright.
Squeeze the glutes at the top without leaning back or arching.
Stay tall, then sit back again.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back as the hips sit back
mistakes.fix: Hinge at the hips with the chest proud and the back flat.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back and arching at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish with the ribs down and the hips under the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing from the low back instead of the glutes
mistakes.fix: Think of driving the hips forward; squeeze the glutes hard at the top.

mistakes.mistake: Knee pain on a hard floor
mistakes.fix: Kneel on a thick mat or a folded towel.

kinematics.norm: Hips flex as they sit back and return to neutral at the top (clinical opinion)
Thighs tilt back toward the heels, knees stay put (clinical opinion)
Knees bend further as the hips sit back (clinical opinion)
Forward hinge with a neutral spine; body-weight hip-extension drills load gluteus maximus (Macadam 2019)

sources.title: GymVisual #15541, Kneeling Hip Thrust (male), video (movement reference)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Knee pain when kneeling: use thick padding, or switch to a standing hip hinge.
Low-back discomfort: shorten the range and keep the back flat.
modify: Toes uncomfortable tucked: rest the tops of the feet on the mat.
